images.title: Two new values, same mean
images.purpose: Shows that adding 7 and 15, one 4 below and one 4 above the mean 11, leaves the mean at 11.
images.composition: One large number line with the four original dots in teal, the two new dots in amber, and two equal arrows from the mean out to the new dots. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A number line from 4 to 25 with 22 evenly spaced short ticks, one at every whole number. Numerals appear only under the ticks at 5, 10 and 24; all other ticks have no numerals. Four teal (#0072B2) dots: two stacked at 5, one at 10, one at 24. Two amber (#E69F00) dots, each drawn with a thin white outline ring to mark it as new: one at 7 with the label '7' above it and one at 15 with the label '15' above it. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) filled triangle under the line at 11 with the label 'mean stays 11' below it. Two equal length grey arrows start at the triangle: one points left to the dot at 7 with the label '4 below' above the arrow, one points right to the dot at 15 with the label '4 above' above the arrow. Exactly 6 dots (4 teal, 2 amber), 1 triangle, 2 arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A value 4 below and a value 4 above the mean cancel, so the mean does not move.
images.description: Shows that adding 7 and 15, one 4 below and one 4 above the mean 11, leaves the mean at 11.
images.context: 5, 5, 10, 24 has sum 44 and mean 11; with 7 and 15 the sum is 66 over 6 values, mean 11.

image_decisions.why: The cancelling of an equal deficit and surplus is easiest to see on the dot plot itself.
